newsitem.title: UK: Excerpts from speech by UK Labour's Brown.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from speech by UK Labour's Brown.

text.p: Following are excerpts from a speech on public spending which Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, will make this afternoon, as reported by the Press Association.
Labour's approach to tax will be based on three core values -- encouraging work and opportunity for all, encouraging investment and savings and promoting a fair society.
"Tony Blair and I have made clear that our programme requires no new spending commitments other than those financed by the windfall tax."
"I can confirm also that we will be making no new commitments in our manifesto which require additional spending."

"After 22 Tory tax rises since 1992 which have hit hard-working families, I want to make it clear we will not increase the basic rate of tax. It is because we understand the importance of work that there will be no return to penal marginal tax rates at the top."
"As a signal of our intentions, I want to make clear that we will not introduce a new top rate of tax."
"Our commitment to fairness means we will cut VAT (value-added tax) on fuel to 5% -- the lowest level allowed. This will be in our manifesto.
"In 1994, I reaffirmed that we would not extend VAT to food, children's clothes and shoes, books and newspapers and public transport fares. That remains the position."

"My tax-cutting ambition is to introduce a new lower starting rate of tax of 10p to encourage people to go back to work and help all hard-working families. This will be matched by a cut in the benefit tapers to ensure that those receiving benefits are also rewarded by the new lower rate."
"I would have liked to have said we could introduce a 10p rate in our first budget. That would be the right thing to do on the grounds of encouraging work, opportunity and fairness.

"But in opposition, without information on the true state of the public finances, I cannot promise that resources are available to do it and therefore I will not make a promise about the timetable for its introduction."
"Today, I have, as promised, made clear the personal tax rate that people will pay under Labour and reaffirmed our existing commitment on that. These are central announcements."
"No sensible and prudent chancellor should go further before we know the economic circumstances and the true state of the public finances.
"It would not be credible to do so. Trust is about making promises you know you can keep and not making promises you know you cannot guarantee to deliver."
